content.comment_body: Hello! Can someone clarify the following paragraph from the [product_name] manual for me? NOTE After switching the power on, the system briefly switches through the outputs on the [product_name] model. With an open circuit, a voltage above 8V may be present for up to around 100 ms; if the circuit is connected to a load, this duration reduces to just microseconds. - What does this mean exactly? Maybe my English isn't strong enough to grasp it fully! - Does this mean that after turning on the [product_name], output devices (such as lamps, contactors, etc.) might switch on temporarily due to a voltage spike? - What does 'open circuit' mean in this context? Is it referring to the circuit program not being loaded? - So, does 'circuit' in the second instance mean 'circuit program'? (... the circuit is loaded... )
An open circuit refers to nothing being connected to the output, or the connected load having very high resistance. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking clarification about a note in the [product_name] manual, particularly regarding 'open circuit' and the effect of output voltage after the system powers on. The user is uncertain if connected output devices might be briefly activated upon startup due to a voltage spike, and has difficulty interpreting the technical terminology, especially relating to the term 'circuit'.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants documentation to clearly explain whether connected output devices will be affected by brief voltage spikes after powering on, and expects unambiguous information to avoid unintended activation of devices.
